question.worked_solution:
We split the integral into the difference of two integrals and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}(\frac{1}{2y}-y)\text{d}y & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{1}^{e}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|y|\,{|}_{1}^{e}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡e-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)-\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1-0)-\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
